examples.ko: 길 한가운데 큰 바위가 가로놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A big rock lies across the middle of the road.

examples.ko: 우리 앞에는 해결할 문제가 많이 가로놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Many problems to solve lie ahead of us.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에는 오랜 오해가 가로놓였어요.
examples.en: A long-standing misunderstanding came between the two people.

examples.ko: 강이 마을 앞에 가로놓여 있어서 다리가 필요해요.
examples.en: A river lies across the front of the village, so a bridge is needed.

examples.ko: 눈앞에 가로놓인 어려움을 하나씩 넘어 보세요.
examples.en: Try to get over the difficulties in front of you one by one.

examples.ko: 길 위에 나무가 가로놓여 있어서 차가 못 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A tree lay across the road, so the cars could not pass.

explain: 사람이 일부러 막는 '가로막다'와 달리, 무언가가 어떤 자리에 가로로 놓여 있는 상태를 말해요. 길 위의 물건뿐 아니라 '문제, 어려움, 오해'가 앞에 있다는 비유로도 많이 써요. 보통 '가로놓여 있다'의 모양으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 우리 앞에 가로놓인 문제를 하나씩 풀어요.
phrases.en: Let's solve the problems in front of us one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가로놓인 + 명사'로 앞을 막고 있는 어려움을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '가로놓인 + noun' refers to a difficulty standing in the way.

phrases.example: 두 나라 사이에 오해가 가로놓여 있어요.
phrases.en: A misunderstanding lies between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 나라 사이의 문제를 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a figurative way to describe a problem between people or countries.

phrases.en: We cross the bridge that lies across the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 가로로 놓인 물건에 쓰는 기본 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the basic meaning, for something physically lying across.

explain_en: Unlike '가로막다', where someone deliberately blocks something, this describes a state in which something simply lies across a place. It is also used figuratively for problems, difficulties or misunderstandings standing in the way. It usually appears as '가로놓여 있다'.

en: to be built; to be constructed

examples.en: A big bridge is being built here.
A new airport was built on the coast.
A park will be built in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 건설된 지 오십 년이 된 건물이에요.
examples.en: It's a building that was built fifty years ago.
When the road is built, travel time gets shorter.
It's a city built by cutting into mountains.

explain: '짓다'는 집·건물에 쓰고, '건설되다'는 다리·도로·댐·도시처럼 큰 시설에 써요. '건설되다'는 집에는 어색해요. '세워지다'도 건물이나 기념비에 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: A new statue was set up in front of the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이나 기념비에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for buildings and monuments.

phrases.example: 이 강에 새 다리가 건설될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: A new bridge is scheduled to be built over this river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 지을 큰 시설을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to announce a large facility to come.

phrases.en: A big road is being built over there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 짓는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is under construction now.

explain_en: '짓다' is for houses and buildings; '건설되다' is for large structures like bridges, roads, dams and cities. It sounds off for a house. '세워지다' also works for buildings and monuments.

dis.h: built as big works like roads or plants

p.n: 건축되다 focuses on the building itself.

examples.en: The hospital isolated the patient in another room.
We have to isolate the patient to prevent infection.

examples.ko: 새로 들어온 고양이를 며칠 동안 격리하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to keep a new cat apart for a few days.

examples.ko: 선생님은 열이 있는 학생을 잠시 격리하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher separated the student with a fever for a while.

examples.ko: 사건 현장을 먼저 격리한 뒤 조사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: They sealed off the scene first and then started the investigation.
Keep dangerous items away from children.

explain: 격리하다는 위험하거나 전염될 수 있는 대상을 따로 떼어 두는 사람이나 기관이 주어예요. '~을/를 ~와/과 격리하다'로 써요. 벌을 주려고 가두는 것은 '가두다'이고, 격리하다는 보호나 예방이 목적이에요.

phrases.example: 아픈 닭을 다른 닭과 따로 뒀어요.
phrases.en: I kept the sick chicken separate from the other chickens.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격리하다'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say 격리하다 in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 선생님이 아픈 아이를 다른 아이들과 분리했어요.
phrases.en: The teacher separated the sick child from the other kids.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격리하다'보다 뜻이 넓어서 물건이나 사람을 떼어 놓을 때 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 격리하다; used for separating both things and people.

phrases.example: 환자를 격리하지 않으면 병이 퍼질 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you don't isolate the patient, the illness can spread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유나 조건을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to state a reason or condition.

explain_en: In 격리하다 the subject is the person or institution that sets apart something dangerous or contagious. The pattern is ~을/를 ~와/과 격리하다. Locking someone up as punishment is 가두다; 격리하다 aims at protection or prevention.

en: to hit against each other; to collide with each other

examples.ko: 두 사람의 의견이 맞부딪쳐서 회의가 길어졌어요.
examples.en: The two people's opinions clashed, so the meeting ran long.
Two bicycles collided head-on in the alley.
The waves crash against the rocks and the spray flies up.

examples.ko: 서로 생각이 맞부딪치면 먼저 이야기를 들어 보세요.
examples.en: When your ideas clash, try listening to each other first.
I nearly ran straight into my friend in the hallway.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 응원 열기가 맞부딪치는 경기였어요.
examples.en: It was a game where the cheering fervor of the two teams collided.

explain: 사람이나 물건이 정면으로 세게 부딪칠 때, 그리고 의견이나 이해관계가 충돌할 때 둘 다 써요. 한쪽이 다른 쪽에 부딪치는 경우에는 그냥 '부딪치다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 두 팀장의 의견이 맞부딪쳐서 결정을 못 했어요.
phrases.en: The two team leaders' opinions clashed, so they couldn't decide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 생각이나 주장이 서로 충돌할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ideas or claims, not people, clash with each other.

phrases.example: 좁은 길에서는 사람들과 맞부딪치지 않게 조심하세요.
phrases.en: On a narrow road, be careful not to collide with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 세게 부딪치는 일을 피하라고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say 'avoid colliding head-on'.

phrases.en: Two cars collided, so the road got blocked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충돌의 결과를 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to link a collision with its result.

explain_en: It is used both when people or objects collide head-on and when opinions or interests clash. When only one side hits the other, plain '부딪치다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Flights were canceled after news of the typhoon moving north.

examples.ko: 태풍의 북상으로 주말에 비가 많이 올 거예요.
examples.en: With the typhoon moving north, it will rain a lot this weekend.

examples.ko: 장마전선이 북상하면서 중부 지방에 비가 내려요.
examples.en: As the rainy front moves north, rain falls in the central region.
The cherry blossom bloom is moving northward.

examples.ko: 태풍이 빠르게 북상 중이라 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The typhoon is moving north fast, so we need to be careful.

examples.ko: 태풍이 북상해서 내일 중부 지방에도 바람이 세게 불어요.
examples.en: The typhoon is moving north, so the wind will blow hard in the central region tomorrow too.

explain: 날씨 뉴스에서 태풍, 장마, 꽃 소식이 위쪽으로 올라올 때 많이 들어요. '태풍이 북상하다'처럼 써요. 반대로 아래쪽으로 내려가는 것은 '남하'예요.

phrases.en: The typhoon is slowly moving north.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북상'을 동사로 쓴 꼴이고, 뉴스에서 아주 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, very common in news reports.

phrases.en: The typhoon is moving north right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 올라오고 있는 상황을 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to say it is happening now.

phrases.en: The typhoon is coming up north.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북상하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy plain-language version of '북상하다'.

explain_en: You hear it often in weather news when a typhoon, rainy front or blossom season moves upward. It is used as '태풍이 북상하다'. The opposite, moving south, is '남하'.

examples.en: The wind blows in from the northwest.
There's a mountain northwest of Seoul.
The ship moved slowly toward the northwest.

examples.ko: 이 지도에서 북서는 오른쪽 위가 아니라 왼쪽 위예요.
examples.en: On this map, northwest is the upper left, not the upper right.
Clouds are rolling in from the northwest.
My house is to the northwest of the school.

explain: '북서'는 방향 이름이라서 보통 '북서쪽', '북서풍'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 같은 방향을 '서북'이라고도 해서, '북동/동북', '남서/서남'처럼 순서를 바꿔 쓰는 말이 많아요.

phrases.en: My house is to the northwest of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북서'에 '쪽'을 붙여 방향을 말할 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 쪽 to 북서 is the most natural way to say the direction.

phrases.en: A cold northwest wind blows in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북서쪽에서 불어오는 바람이에요. 날씨 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A wind blowing from the northwest, common in weather talk.

phrases.en: Please go in the northwest direction on the map.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북서'와 같은 방향인데 두 글자의 순서를 바꾼 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same direction as 북서 with the two characters swapped.

explain_en: '북서' is a compass term and is usually followed by another word, as in '북서쪽' or '북서풍'. The same direction can also be called '서북', and many directions can be said in either order, such as '북동/동북' and '남서/서남'.

en: remote mountain area; backwoods; isolated mountainous area

examples.ko: 산간벽지에는 아직 병원이 없는 마을도 있어요.
examples.en: There are still remote mountain villages without a hospital.
The teacher taught children at a school in a remote mountain area.

examples.ko: 눈이 오면 산간벽지는 길이 끊기기도 해요.
examples.en: When it snows, roads in remote mountain areas are sometimes cut off.

examples.ko: 산간벽지로 가는 버스는 하루에 두 번뿐이에요.
examples.en: The bus to the remote mountain area runs only twice a day.
The government decided to expand internet networks in remote mountain areas.
Having grown up in the backwoods, he found the city unfamiliar.

explain: 산이 많고 교통이 불편한 외진 곳을 말해요. 뉴스나 정책 이야기에서 '도서벽지'와 함께 나오는 일이 많아요. 비슷한 말로 '오지'가 있어요.

phrases.en: The road to the remote village is narrow and rough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산간벽지와 비슷한 말이지만 산이 아니어도 외딴 곳에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 산간벽지, but it can be used for remote places that are not mountainous.

phrases.en: My grandmother lives in a remote mountain area, so the hospital is far.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통이 불편한 외진 곳에 산다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone lives in a secluded place with poor transportation.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a remote mountain area

phrases.en: The internet reaches even remote islands and rural areas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 섬과 외진 시골을 함께 말하는 말로 '산간벽지'와 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to islands and remote rural areas together, often appearing alongside 산간벽지.

explain_en: It refers to remote places with many mountains and poor transport. In news and policy talk it often appears alongside '도서벽지' (remote islands and areas). A similar word is '오지'.

examples.en: There are many mountains in the northwest of this country.
It will snow in the northwestern region today.

examples.ko: 서북부 지역은 아침에 안개가 자주 껴요.
examples.en: The northwest area often has fog in the morning.
Our school is in the northwest part of the city.
Where do I take the bus going to the northwest?
Try finding the northwest part on the map.

explain: 어떤 지역의 서북쪽 부분을 말하고, '북서쪽'이라고도 해요. 날씨 예보나 지리 설명에서 지역 이름과 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My house is northwest of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서북부'와 같은 방향이지만 지역보다 방향을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same direction as 서북부, but used more for direction than for a region.

phrases.en: Tomorrow it will rain in the northwestern region.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 예보에서 가장 자주 듣는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The phrase you hear most in weather forecasts.

phrases.en: There are many parks in the northwest of this city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에는'을 붙여 그 지역의 특징을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에는 introduces a feature of that area.

explain_en: It refers to the northwest part of an area, and people also say '북서쪽'. It is often used with place names in weather forecasts and geography explanations.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 소각장이 우리 동네에 생긴다고 해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried because they say a waste incineration plant is going to be built in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 소각장에서 나오는 열로 근처 아파트에 난방을 해요.
examples.en: They heat nearby apartments with the heat from the incineration plant.
The residents are opposing the construction of the incineration plant.

examples.ko: 소각장은 매연 때문에 늘 논란이 돼요.
examples.en: Incineration plants are always controversial because of the smoke.
A truck carrying waste to the incineration plant is passing by.

examples.ko: 공장 옆 소각장 때문에 냄새가 난다는 민원이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many complaints that the incineration plant next to the factory causes a smell.

explain: 쓰레기를 태워서 처리하는 곳이고, 땅에 묻어서 처리하는 곳은 '매립지'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '소각장 건설 반대'처럼 주민 갈등 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Residents gathered over the construction of the incineration plant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 주민 갈등과 함께 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in news about resident disputes.

phrases.en: I'm worried about the air around the incineration plant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소각장 가까이의 환경이나 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the environment or life near the plant.

phrases.en: Sorted trash is burned at the incineration plant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 어디서 처리하는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain where trash gets disposed of.
phrases.en_equiv: to burn at the incineration plant

explain_en: This is a place that disposes of trash by burning it, while a place that buries trash is called '매립지'. In the news it often appears in stories about resident conflicts, such as opposition to building an incineration plant.

examples.ko: 서울 이남 지역은 오늘 날씨가 맑아요.
examples.en: The weather is clear in areas south of Seoul today.
I live south of the Han River.

examples.ko: 이 기차는 대전 이남으로는 가지 않아요.
examples.en: This train doesn't go south of Daejeon.

examples.ko: 이 강 이남은 새로 만든 도시예요.
examples.en: The area south of this river is a newly built city.

examples.ko: 충청도 이남에서는 비가 많이 내릴 거예요.
examples.en: It will rain a lot south of Chungcheong.

examples.ko: 이 도로 이남은 공사 때문에 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: The road south of here is jammed because of construction.

explain: 이남은 어떤 곳을 기준으로 그 남쪽 지역을 말해서 항상 '서울 이남', '한강 이남'처럼 앞에 기준 장소가 붙어요. 반대는 '이북'이에요. 그냥 '남쪽'이라고 하면 방향만 말하고 기준 장소가 없어도 돼요.

phrases.example: 대구 이남 지역에는 비가 많이 와요.
phrases.en: It rains a lot in the area south of Daegu.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이남'에 '지역'을 붙여서 기준 장소 아래쪽 전체 지역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 지역 (area) to 이남 refers to the whole region south of a reference place.

phrases.en: I'm heading down to the area south of Daejeon this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준 장소보다 남쪽으로 이동한다는 뜻이고, 이남 뒤에 '으로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means moving to the area south of a reference place; 으로 follows 이남.

phrases.en: It didn't snow south of Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이남과 비슷하지만 '남쪽'은 방향만 말해서 기준 장소가 없어도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 이남, but 남쪽 only gives a direction and doesn't need a reference place.

explain_en: 이남 means the region south of a reference point, so it always follows a place, as in '서울 이남' or '한강 이남'. Its opposite is '이북'. Plain '남쪽' just means the direction and needs no reference place.

examples.en: The old building was demolished.
All the signs beside the road were taken down.

examples.ko: 불법 건물은 다음 달에 철거될 예정이에요.
examples.en: The illegal building is set to be torn down next month.
A park will be built where it was demolished.

examples.ko: 낡은 아파트가 철거되는 동안 소음이 심했어요.
examples.en: The noise was bad while the old apartment was being demolished.
As the tents were removed, the square became spacious again.

explain: 철거되다는 건물, 시설, 간판처럼 세워져 있던 것이 치워져 없어질 때 써요. 철거 현장, 철거 공사 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 물건을 정리해서 버리는 '치우다'와 달리 구조물을 뜯어낸다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 철거된 건물 자리에 작은 공원이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A small park appeared where the demolished building used to be.
phrases.nuance_ko: '철거되다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 이미 없어진 것을 말하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing something that has already been removed.

phrases.example: 낡은 집이 헐려서 새 아파트가 들어와요.
phrases.en: The old house is being torn down and a new apartment building is coming in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '철거되다'와 비슷하지만 말할 때 쓰는 더 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 철거되다 but an easier, more spoken expression.

phrases.en: This bridge is scheduled to be demolished next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 예정이다'를 붙여 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -(으)ㄹ 예정이다, it describes a future plan.

explain_en: 철거되다 is used when something that stood, such as a building, facility or sign, is cleared away. It appears with words like 철거 현장 and 철거 공사. Unlike 치우다, which means tidying things away, it feels like tearing down a structure.

examples.en: The train slipped on the snowy track and derailed.
Service was delayed because a train derailed.

examples.ko: 아이가 탈선하지 않도록 부모가 관심을 가져 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Parents need to pay attention so their child doesn't go astray.

examples.ko: 그는 한때 나쁜 친구들과 어울리며 탈선했던 적이 있어요.
examples.en: He once went astray, hanging out with bad friends.

examples.ko: 이야기가 자꾸 탈선해서 원래 주제로 돌아가야겠어요.
examples.en: The conversation keeps going off track, so we should return to the original topic.

examples.ko: 청소년이 탈선하면 주변에서 먼저 따뜻하게 이야기를 들어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When a teenager goes astray, the people around should first listen warmly.

explain: 기차가 선로를 벗어난다는 뜻과, 사람이 바른 길에서 벗어나 엇나가거나 이야기가 옆길로 샌다는 비유로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 비유로는 '엇나가다', '삐뚤어지다', '옆길로 새다'도 많이 말해요. 사람에게 쓰면 꽤 무거운 말이에요.

phrases.en: A train derailment accident happened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차가 선로를 벗어난 사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an accident where a train leaves the tracks.

phrases.en: The conversation keeps going off topic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기가 본래 주제에서 벗어날 때 일상에서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in daily speech when talk drifts off the main topic.
phrases.en_equiv: to go off on a tangent

phrases.en: I went a little astray during my teenage years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 바른 길에서 벗어나는 비유에 쓰고, '탈선하다'보다 덜 무거워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people straying from the right path; less heavy than '탈선하다'.

explain_en: It means a train leaving the rails, and figuratively a person leaving the right path or a conversation going off on a tangent. In daily conversation, '엇나가다', '삐뚤어지다' and '옆길로 새다' are also common for the figurative sense. Used about a person, it is quite a heavy word.

examples.en: Applications for the event poured in all at once.
Orders flooded in, so packing got very delayed.
When visitors surge, the site slows down.
Calls with questions will flood in tomorrow.
I woke up to the sound of a motorcycle racing recklessly.
Requests are pouring in, so the server is shaky.

explain: '주문이 폭주하다', '접속이 폭주하다'처럼 한꺼번에 너무 많이 몰릴 때 써요. 또 차나 오토바이가 위험하게 마구 달릴 때도 써요. 주어는 주문, 신청, 문의 같은 말이 많아요.

phrases.en: Inquiries poured in when the new product came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주문' 말고도 문의, 신청처럼 한꺼번에 몰리는 것에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for inquiries and applications, not just orders.

phrases.example: 표를 팔기 시작하자 접속이 폭주해서 사이트가 멈췄어요.
phrases.en: Traffic surged when tickets went on sale, and the site froze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이트에 사람이 한꺼번에 몰릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people hit a website at once.

phrases.en: The reckless riders make noise every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오토바이를 위험하게 몰고 다니는 사람들을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for people who ride motorcycles recklessly.

explain_en: Used when too much arrives at once, as in '주문이 폭주하다' or '접속이 폭주하다'. It also describes a car or motorcycle racing dangerously. Typical subjects are 주문, 신청, and 문의.
